nodes.text: Peace on your road, traveler. The hall is open — it always is. Sit, if your feet have opinions. I'm *Ansel*. I keep the lamps, the benches, and the book.

choices.text: What do the Waykeepers believe, exactly?

nodes.text: Nothing you'd need a robe for. A lit lamp is a *promise* — somebody made it, somebody keeps it, somebody walks safer because of it. We keep the lamps. That's the whole creed. It fits on a lamppost, which is rather the point.

The registry. Every soul who walks north through our gate signs it, or I sign for them. Most names take a homecoming mark within the year. Some never do. On feast nights I read the unmarked names to the braziers. Somebody should say them aloud, somewhere, once a season. It may as well be me.

Founded on the mountain, in the bad years after Silverfall sealed its deeps and the roads went feral. Marshal Kestrel's grandmother built the first waystation out of her own crew's wages — the Marshal keeps the order still, from the chapter house up there. Sergeants at the stations, Edda at the Last Lamp, and me at the southern end. I lit lamps on the High Road for eleven years. My knees keep the record, in wet weather especially.
Peace on your road. Sign the book before you walk north — humor a keeper's arithmetic.
